modules.title: Python Debugger (pdb & breakpoint()): Stepping, Frames & Bug Hunting
modules.subtitle: Stop sprinkling print() everywhere—pause execution live, inspect variables, and trace stack frames cleanly.
modules.summary: Master Python's built-in `breakpoint()` and `pdb` commands (`n`, `s`, `c`, `p`, `w`, `u`, `d`, conditional `b`), then hunt down 3 real bugs in Neovim.

sections.title: 1.1 Core `pdb` Navigation & Inspection Commands
sections.body: Drop `breakpoint()` on any line of Python 3.7+ code to pause right inside `pdb`. Unlike `print()`, you can evaluate live expressions, step line-by-line, jump up and down the call stack, and even mutate variables on the fly to test fixes.
sections.code_example:
n  (next)      -> execute current line; step OVER function calls
s  (step)      -> step INTO the function called on this line
r  (return)    -> continue until the current function returns
c  (continue)  -> run until next breakpoint
l / ll         -> list source lines around current line (ll = whole function)
p expr / pp    -> print (or pretty-print) any Python expression
w  (where)     -> print full call stack trace
u / d          -> move UP (caller) or DOWN (callee) stack frames
b 42, x > 10   -> set conditional breakpoint at line 42 when x > 10

sections.title: 1.2 Post-Mortem & Pytest Debugging (`--pdb`)
sections.body: When a script or test crashes deep in a pipeline, run `pytest -s --pdb` (drops you into `pdb` at the exact crashing frame!) or `python -m pdb -c continue script.py` to launch post-mortem inspection without even editing the file.
sections.code_example:
# Drop into pdb automatically on the first failing test:
pytest -s --pdb

# Run script until an unhandled exception, then inspect live state:
python3 -m pdb -c continue buggy_eval.py

spec.question: You are paused in `pdb` on `score = compute_f1(preds, labels)`. You want to enter `compute_f1` and trace its internal lines. Which command do you type?
spec.explanation: `s` (step) steps INTO `compute_f1`. `n` (next) executes `compute_f1` in one shot and lands on the next line of the caller.

spec.template:
# Pause execution in Python 3.7+:
___()

spec.explanation: `breakpoint()` triggers `pdb` (respecting `PYTHONBREAKPOINT`), and `w` (`where` / `bt`) shows the full stack trace.

activities.title: Participation Activity: Trace a Classic Mutable Default Bug

spec.prompt: Use your debugger mental model to trace `bucket` across two calls to this buggy function.

steps.note: Default list `[]` is allocated ONCE when `def record` executes—NOT per call!
`first` and `second` point to the exact same list, so `len(first)` is now 2!

spec.explanation: Always default mutable params to `None` (`bucket: list | None = None`) and initialize `if bucket is None: bucket = []` inside the function.

activities.title: Interactive Debugger Simulation: Step Through `buggy_total()` in `(Pdb)`

spec.prompt: `buggy_total([10, 20, 30])` returns `30` instead of `60`! Use the live `(Pdb)` prompt below: step through the loop with `n` (or `s`), inspect the accumulator with `p total`, and print the call stack with `w` to spot the bug.
spec.explanation: Stepping with `n` and inspecting `p total` exposed that line 4 assigns `total = n` (overwriting `total` on every iteration) instead of accumulating with `total += n`. Running `w` confirmed the call path `<module> -> run_eval -> buggy_total`.

activities.title: Neovim Debugging Lab: Hunt 3 Bugs in `buggy_eval.py` Using `pdb`

spec.instructions:
`buggy_eval.py` has 3 sneaky bugs:
1. `collect_scores(score, history=[])` leaks state across separate calls.
2. `top_k_average(scores, k)` has an off-by-one slice & fails to sort descending.
3. `safe_ratio(hits, total)` crashes with `ZeroDivisionError` when `total == 0` (should return `0.0`).

Practice dropping `breakpoint()` and running `python3 buggy_eval.py` in a split terminal to inspect values in `pdb`, fix all 3 bugs, remove `breakpoint()`, and hit `:w`!
spec.test_code:
from buggy_eval import collect_scores, top_k_average, safe_ratio

def test_collect_scores_isolated():
    a = collect_scores(0.8)
    b = collect_scores(0.9)
    assert a == [0.8]
    assert b == [0.9]
    assert collect_scores(0.5, [0.1]) == [0.1, 0.5]

def test_top_k_average():
    assert top_k_average([0.4, 0.9, 0.7], 2) == 0.8
    assert top_k_average([0.2, 0.6], 5) == 0.4
    assert top_k_average([], 2) == 0.0

def test_safe_ratio():
    assert safe_ratio(3, 4) == 0.75
    assert safe_ratio(0, 0) == 0.0
hints: In `collect_scores`, use `history: list[float] | None = None` and `history = [] if history is None else history`.
In `top_k_average`, use `sorted(scores, reverse=True)[:k]` (remember `k` may exceed `len(scores)` so divide by `len(top)`!).
In `safe_ratio`, return `0.0` when `total == 0`. Remember to remove any `breakpoint()` before saving!

modules.title: Multi-Stack Debugging: Bash `set -x`, `gdb`, Node & Playwright Traces
modules.subtitle: Diagnose shell scripts, C++ crashes, JS async bugs, and flaky E2E tests systematically.
modules.summary: Learn the universal debugging toolkit across Bash (`set -x`), C++ (`g++ -g` + `gdb`), Node (`--inspect`), and Playwright (`--debug` / Trace Viewer).

sections.title: 2.1 Tracing Bash, C++ (gdb) & Playwright
sections.body: Every runtime has a first-class tracer: Bash prints every expanded command with `bash -x script.sh` (set `PS4='+$LINENO: '` to include line numbers!). C++ requires compiling with `-g` so `gdb` can map crash addresses to source lines (`bt` for backtrace). Playwright's `--debug` opens the live Inspector where you step through every locator.
sections.code_example:
# Bash execution trace with line numbers:
PS4='+line $LINENO: ' bash -x deploy.sh

# C++ debug symbols + gdb backtrace:
g++ -std=c++20 -g -O0 main.cpp -o app && gdb -ex run -ex bt ./app

# Playwright step-by-step inspector:
npx playwright test --debug

activities.title: Participation Activity: C++ Debug Symbols for `gdb`

spec.question: Which `g++` flag embeds source file names, line numbers, and variable names so `gdb` can show readable stack traces?
spec.explanation: `-g` emits DWARF debug info; pairing `-g -O0` prevents the compiler from optimizing away local variables while stepping.
spec.hint: Short single-letter flag standing for debug info.

activities.title: Neovim Debugging Lab: Trace & Fix a Broken Bash Script (`bash -x`)

spec.instructions:
`sum_col.sh <file>` is supposed to sum column 2 of a CSV file (skipping the header line) even when the filename contains spaces—but it has 2 bugs!
Try running `bash -x sum_col.sh` on a test file, fix the unquoted variable + awk logic in Neovim, and save `:w` to verify.

starter_files.sum_col.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
file=$1
# BUG 1: unquoted $file breaks filenames with spaces!
# BUG 2: doesn't skip header or split by comma properly
awk '{s += $2} END {print s}' $file

checks.name: sums CSV column 2 with spaces in filename

hints: In awk, pass `-F,` and skip line 1 with `NR > 1 { s += $2 } END { print s + 0 }`.
